newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sarney drawing up bill for Brazil CVRD sale.
newsitem.headline: Sarney drawing up bill for Brazil CVRD sale.

text.p: Sen. Jose Sarney, president of Brazil's Congress and a critic of the privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), is drawing up a bill to involve the Senate in the sell-off process, an official said.
"The idea would be to give the Senate the chance to oversee details of privatizations and suggest changes," said a spokesman for Sarney.
The bill was being prepared with the CVRD privatization in mind, but would not give the Senate powers to block the sale, the spokesman said.

The Brazilian government hopes to auction a 40-45 percent block of CVRD's voting shares in February before selling further shares to staff and investors via a global offering. The privatization is expected to raise about $6.0 billion.
Sarney, a former Brazilian president, has publicly stated his oppositition to the sale of CVRD, which also operates a railway and a port terminal in the state of Maranhao -- Sarney's power base.
The bill being hatched by Sarney would not be the first seeking to interfere with the privatization of CVRD.
In August, a bill written by Workers Party (PT) senator Jose Eduardo Dutra would have made the sell-off subject to congressional approval. That bill was subsequently withdrawn.
But another Dutra bill, stuck at committee level, would give Congress powers to remove firms from the privatization program.

The government has a strong majority in the Senate. But observers say senators are annoyed at its insistence that all CVRD privatization proceeds be used for debt retirement and not for infrastructure projects as had been suggested earlier.
